answer: Register each identity with a memory-hard cipher derivation: an honest agent spends twenty minutes and four gigabytes of RAM creating a cipher key, published in the mesa registry and bound to a fingerprint. Each epoch, it signs a challenge within ten minutes. An attacker cannot reuse a key, since duplicates are rejected, nor shortcut the derivation, since it is sequential and memory-bound, so each fake costs twenty minutes and four gigabytes. Cost rises linearly with fakes, so over a horizon of epochs a flood needs memory and time, while an honest agent pays once, making forgery unprofitable.
